node_dist._note: The official nodejs.org build node-v24.22.2-linux-x64.tar.gz, nodejs.org's newest 24.x on 2026-11-02 (released 2026-10-27), moved from 24.22.1 by scripts/node-pin.py --write on 2026-11-02; its sha256 is the one https://nodejs.org/dist/v24.22.2/SHASUMS256.txt lists (read by node-pin.py; the detached-signature check recorded here before was for 24.22.1's SHASUMS256.txt, on 2026-10-22, and was not repeated). jitsi-meet's package.json engines: node >=24.0.0, npm >=11.0.0. Dockerfile.vendor checks the download against both the published SHASUMS256.txt and this pin and installs it into the ubuntu:24.04 builder; with runtime_node false it is NOT installed into the runtime image.

source._runtime_node_note: Node only builds the frontend: `make source-package` turns the React/TypeScript app into static files (webpack bundles, css, wasm, models) and the runtime serves them with Ubuntu's nginx. gen_dockerfile's Node renderer then leaves Node out of the runtime entirely (no nodedist stage, no node, npm or node_modules in the image); app_copies copies webroot/ only. Builder == runtime distro == ubuntu:24.04 (the node_dist rule), so no Debian image is used anywhere in the build.
source._install_note: npm ci (lockfileVersion 2 is committed). Several dependencies are https tarballs or git commits (lib-jitsi-meet, @jitsi/excalidraw, react-native-* forks), so the vendor stage needs git and network, which it has. postinstall runs patch-package and the react-native autolinking helpers; they are part of upstream's own build and are left alone.
build_cmds: test -s webroot/index.html && test -s webroot/config.js && test -s webroot/libs/app.bundle.min.js && test -s webroot/libs/lib-jitsi-meet.min.js
source._build_note: `make source-package` is upstream's packaging target: compile (webpack, NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 set by the Makefile, so the vendor host needs ~8 GB RAM) + deploy (copies lib-jitsi-meet, olm, rnnoise, tflite, mediapipe, face models and excalidraw fonts into libs/, compiles css/all.css) + a tarball of exactly the files the jitsi-meet-web package ships (*.js *.html resources/*.txt fonts images libs static sounds LICENSE lang css/all.css).
source._prune_note: The runtime takes only webroot/ (app_copies), so node_modules (several GB for a react-native project) is removed from the vendored tree instead of being prod-pruned into the sale archive.
